Key facts sheet · Life in the UK
Based on the handbook’s own summary of key material and facts, checked against the main text. Use it for a last read before the test.
Magna Carta (1215): limited the king’s power and established that the king is subject to the law
Statute of Rhuddlan (1284): Edward I annexed Wales to the Crown of England
Act for the Government of Wales (reign of Henry VIII): formally united England and Wales
Bill of Rights (1689): rights of Parliament, limits of the king’s power; monarch must be Protestant
Act of Union (1707): Kingdom of Great Britain (Treaty of Union in Scotland)
Act of Union ({#}): Ireland joins in {#}; new Union Flag
Slave trade abolished (1807); Emancipation Act (1833) abolished slavery in the Empire
Reform Act (1832): abolished pocket and rotten boroughs; more voters
Human Rights Act {#}: brought the ECHR into UK law
Romans: AD 43–410 (about 400 years). Hadrian’s Wall kept out the Picts
Middle Ages: 1066–1485, almost constant war incl. the Crusades and the Hundred Years War
Elizabethan period (late 1500s): patriotism, exploration, poetry and drama
The Enlightenment (18th century): Adam Smith, David Hume, James Watt
Industrial Revolution (18th–19th centuries): over half the world’s cotton cloth, coal and iron
Victorian Age (1837–1901): the largest empire in world history
1066 Hastings: William of Normandy defeats Harold (Bayeux Tapestry)
{#} Bannockburn: Robert the Bruce defeats the English
{#} Agincourt: Henry V beats the French
1455–1485 Wars of the Roses: Lancaster (red) v York (white); ends at Bosworth Field
1642–1646 Civil war: Roundheads (Parliament) v Cavaliers (king); Marston Moor and Naseby
1805 Trafalgar: Nelson; 1815 Waterloo: Wellington defeats Napoleon
1939–1945 Second World War: Dunkirk and Battle of Britain (1940), D-Day (6 June 1944)
{#} Black Death: one third of England dies
By {#} English the language of court and Parliament
{#}s Church of England founded by Henry VIII
{#} James VI of Scotland becomes James I
{#} Great Plague; {#} Great Fire of London
{#} NHS founded; {#} UK joins the EEC
1998 Good Friday Agreement; 1999 Scottish Parliament and Welsh Assembly
2022 Charles III becomes king; 2024 Labour wins under Keir Starmer
Alfred the Great: united the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, defeated the Vikings
Henry VIII: six wives; broke from Rome; Wales united with England
Elizabeth I: Protestant; Armada; balanced religious views
Oliver Cromwell: Lord Protector of the republic
Sir Francis Drake: Armada; sailed around the world in the Golden Hind
Isaac Newton: gravity; white light is the colours of the rainbow
Robert Burns: Scottish poet, Auld Lang Syne
Sake Dean Mahomet: first curry house ({#}); shampooing
Isambard Kingdom Brunel: Great Western Railway, bridges, tunnels, ships
Clement Attlee: PM {#}–{#}; NHS and welfare state
Margaret Thatcher: first woman PM; longest-serving PM of the 20th century
Mary Peters: Olympic gold {#}; promoted sport in NI
Dylan Thomas: Welsh poet, Under Milk Wood
Sir Arthur Conan Doyle: Scottish author of Sherlock Holmes
